reason: Primary source identity is confirmed (Ghelfi et al., 2020, DOI 10.1177/2515245919881152, OSF https://osf.io/5ygsp), and the neutral description plus p. 9 locator identify the bitter-versus-control moral-wrongness contrast (published PDF pp. 8-9, Fig. 1). Although the bitter-versus-control LMER contrast was statistically significant among naive participants, the confirmatory meta-analytic 95% CI included zero, the effect was significantly smaller than d33% and equivalent to 0 +/- 0.30, and the authors explicitly conclude that the results failed to support the hypothesis.

location: Confirmatory Analyses (All Participants), manuscript pp. 24-25 (published PDF pp. 9-10, Fig. 2); Discussion, manuscript pp. 33-34
quote: The overall effect for bitter versus sweet was negligible ... Overall, we found little to no support for Eskine and colleagues’ (2011) conclusions.
reason: The neutral description and p. 10 locator identify the bitter-versus-sweet moral-wrongness contrast (published PDF pp. 9-10, Fig. 2). Across the confirmatory meta-analysis, one-sided small-telescopes and equivalence tests, and LMER models, the bitter-versus-sweet contrast was negligible and in the opposite of the predicted direction, and the authors explicitly conclude that the replication failed to support the original finding.
